acceptance_criteria: Core k-eff at 123.576 cm within 500-1000 pcm of RMC 1.004288, with a V&V record stating the data-library offset, a measured Shannon-entropy convergence trace, and a measured runtime. NOT closed on child count - see the op-6w0/op-cel over-closing failure recorded in CLAUDE.md.
description:
Reproduce Li, Yu & Wei (2014) HTR2014-51207 HTR-10 whole-core k-eff at the 123.576 cm critical loading height (RMC 1.004288, MCNP 1.0033) as a code-to-code comparison in outram-mc-libs.

Maintainer decisions 2026-09-17: ENDF/B-VIII.0 with the VII.0 offset STATED not hidden; 500-1000 pcm gate; reproduce the paper's hex-prism packing recipe exactly (no DEM); DELTA tracking inside the core only with SURFACE tracking everywhere else; the hybrid API lands separately first with its own V&V; reflector from IAEA-TECDOC-1382 Table 4-3 homogenised zones; no pebble-level OpenMC oracle.

Why hybrid: a B4C control rod sets the majorant for the whole domain, so virtual-collision rejection explodes even out in the graphite. This crate has already measured that pathology - bounding over the whole material table including the undiluted kernel multiplied virtual collisions by ~25x at the U-238 resonances (src/dh_universe.rs:101-108).

Plan: ~/.claude/plans/wondrous-gathering-whale.md

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
DE-RISKING, before any Phase 1 or Phase 2 code.

1. DEPTH-3 LATTICE NAVIGATION WORKS -- risk retired (commit 1eb1723eb0). The core model is a hex bed lattice -> pebble universe -> TRISO lattice, three levels, and NOTHING in the crate had ever tested lattice-inside-lattice: the deepest case asserted anywhere was depth 2. Now gated by tests/nested_lattice_depth3.rs, shaped like HTR-10 rather than like a convenient abstraction. locate returns 3 levels with the right lattice ids and tile indices, and -- the part that matters -- a particle streaming inside the nested lattice stops at the INNER tile edge (0.050000 cm) rather than sailing past it. op-6tz.34's under-count does not recur one level deeper.

   This retires DEPTH only. SCALE is untouched: the largest lattice ever built here is 37 hex tiles against ~24,000 needed.

2. THE B4C MAJORANT ARGUMENT IS NOW MEASURED -- 26.3x at thermal (commit 9e1241327b). See op-867c.5 for the method and the full energy structure. Phase 1 is justified by a number rather than an analogy.

Both were cheap and both could have changed the plan. Neither did.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
EIGENVALUE ATTEMPTED 2026-09-17 -- IT RETURNS k = 0. The epic stays OPEN; its acceptance criterion (core k-eff within 500-1000 pcm of RMC 1.004288) is not met.

All 17 children are closed and the infrastructure is built, gated and pushed. The eigenvalue example assembles a four-level explicit-TRISO core, engages the hybrid dispatch, and reports -- but computes nothing.

THREE INDEPENDENT ELIMINATIONS, each committed with its diagnostic:

  geometry   20,000 uniform probes, 0 lost, all eight materials reached, four-level descent, Delta inside the bed and Surface in the reflector (htr10_locate_probe)
  tracker    the SAME geometry with surface tracking only gives the same k = 0, with ZERO virtual collisions, in 1.8 s vs 80 s (OUTRAM_HTR10_SURFACE=1)
  materials  UO2 kernel nu-fission 5.691 cm^-1 at thermal, non-fuel layers correctly zero (htr10_material_check)

The tracker elimination is the one worth noting: it was only possible BECAUSE op-867c.7 had already established hybrid == surface at 0.62 sigma. A disagreement would have implicated the tracker; the agreement implicates the model. That is an equivalence gate used in anger.

The 2.82e9 virtual collisions (18,801/history) were a SYMPTOM, not the cause -- priced at ~22 rejections per real collision, matching the ~25x already measured for an undiluted kernel. Chasing them would have been chasing the wrong thing.

k = 0 EXACTLY is the strongest remaining clue and argues against "core too small": a subcritical multiplying system gives a small k, not zero. Zero means generation 0 banked no fission neutron at all and the driver broke on an empty bank.

NEXT: check whether source neutrons reach a kernel. It is 0.025 % of the bed by volume, so a history must both moderate and find one. Suspects: MAX_EVENTS truncating histories, or the source spectrum sitting above the thermal window where that volume fraction is survivable. Hypothesis, not finding.

title: HTR-10 RMC benchmark: hybrid delta/surface tracking and a full-core criticality model

description: Follow-up to op-4542 (Wakao exponent fix, landed 2026-08-11). crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/pre_built_components/non_insulated_porous_media_fluid_components/preprocessing/ciet_heater_v2.rs:~391 (ciet_heater_v2_get_therminol_node_twisted_tape_conductance) builds Reynolds from the hydraulic diameter (0.5776 in) and feeds it to the Wakao correlation, which is defined on particle/pebble diameter with superficial velocity. The original author flagged this in-code ('need to convert hydraulic diameter to an equivalent spherical diameter ... live with it for the time being'). The op-4542 exponent fix does not address this; measured effect of the whole Wakao path on CIET heater steady-state outlet temps is <0.01 K (regression pins recorded pre-fix still pass at 0.01 K tolerance post-fix, 2026-08-11), so severity is low, but the modelling inconsistency should be resolved or documented as a deliberate approximation. Same hazard exists for any future component that reuses WakaoData with a non-particle diameter.
title: tuas: CIET heater v2 feeds hydraulic-diameter Reynolds into particle-diameter Wakao correlation

description: Maintainer split 2026-09-12: neutronics is TWO papers. Part II = prelim NJOY data prep + non-doubly-heterogeneous outram-mc (ICSBEP Godiva/Jemima/HST-009/LCT-008 + boron series + tracking-method equivalence + thermal-kernel moments). Part III = double heterogeneity (FHR pebble explicit TRISO vs ring-RPT). Datasets already partitioned: docs/paper-datasets/part2-data-and-transport/ and part3-double-heterogeneity/. Editorial work remaining: the 1547-line ring_rpt_vs_openmc.md interleaves both - Results/Interpretation carry the pebble material, the mechanism table and ICSBEP rows carry Part II's. mechanism_elimination.csv stays with Part III but its ICSBEP/NJOY rows must be captioned as results IMPORTED from Part II, not re-derived (self-plagiarism risk). PUBLICATION ORDER: Part II first, get its arXiv id, then Part III cites it - Part III's +4004 pcm absolute bias is explained by Part II's LCT-008 finding. Part III's headline (RPT-explicit +226+-316) is a model DIFFERENCE so the data bias largely cancels - say so explicitly and early.
title: Paper Part III: split the doubly-heterogeneous material out of the ring_rpt record

design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


Once the public Rust API stabilizes, run a fresh Haiku agent:

> Build a small steady flowsheet in which a hydrocarbon stream is evaluated
> with Peng-Robinson, exchanges heat with an IAPWS water/steam stream, then
> crosses into another thermodynamic package. Preserve mass and energy and
> print the bridge diagnostics. Use only the public API/rustdoc/prelude.

Record API friction, fix genuine defects, re-run with a fresh agent, then
**independently verify the physics**.

> **If it is too complex for Haiku to use correctly through the public API, it
> is a bad API.**

**Haiku friction logs are API evidence, not automatically validation
evidence.** In #58, four of six agent reports carried a confident wrong physics
claim, each caught only against a published value.

Note the crate currently has **no prelude**, which this epic's public surface
will need — see #75.

Add a public tutorial demonstrating the corrected workflow.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.
title: MultiThermo: Public tutorial and Haiku dogfood

description:
Found 2026-08-11 while fixing op-cv1c (the half-open 100 MPa region-router range).

FACT, measured, not inferred. With the op-cv1c router fix in place these two previously-#[ignore]d IF97 verification-table tests PASS:

  interfaces::tests_and_examples::pt_flash_steam_table::single_phase_table_240_bar_to_1000_bar::single_phase_table_2_to_750_degc_1000_bar
  interfaces::tests_and_examples::ps_flash_steam_table::single_phase_table_240_bar_to_1000_bar::single_phase_table_2_to_750_degc_1000_bar

Both carry the ignore reason 'to implement in next major version'. 1000 bar IS 100 MPa, i.e. exactly the pressure the router rejected, so the reason was almost certainly a mis-diagnosis of this bug.

CAUSALITY VERIFIED by stashing the router fix and re-running: with the old half-open ranges both FAIL; with the fix both pass. Command used:
  cargo test --release -p tampines-steam-tables --lib -- --ignored single_phase_table_2_to_750_degc_1000_bar

PROPOSAL (maintainer's call, not done by the agent that found it): drop the #[ignore] from both, and update the ignored-test table in crates/tampines-steam-tables/CLAUDE.md accordingly (it currently lists 14 ignored tests; this would take it to 12).

STILL FAILING at 1000 bar, so NOT candidates:
  ph_flash_steam_table::single_phase_table_1000_bar::single_phase_table_2_to_750_degc — no longer 'out of bounds'; now a genuine accuracy failure at the 2 degC row (entropy left=0.019946 right=0.020113561381955317, max_relative=7e-3). The ignore reason in CLAUDE.md ('at 1000 bar, ph flashing goes out of bounds, yet to debug') is now stale and should be reworded to the accuracy finding.
  hs_flash_steam_table::single_phase_table_1000_bar::single_phase_table_2_to_750_degc — panics in ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs: the hs flash produces p = 100000837.65614447 Pa, genuinely above the 100 MPa ceiling. Separate bug (see the hs-flash backoff bead).
title: tampines-steam-tables: two 1000-bar flash-table tests now pass — candidates to un-ignore
